audit_findings.title: Completed acquisition is missing from both the earnings perimeter and post-deal balance sheet
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes operating OE, cash, assumed liabilities, debt and potentially diluted shares, but the valuation combines pre-acquisition OE and the June 27 pre-closing bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The purchase price for possible acquisitions of businesses and assets might be paid from cash, borrowings, or through the issuance of common stock or other securities, or a combination of these methods.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: Homes Direct closed in August 2026 before the September 6 valuation date. Omitted acquired earnings may understate value, while spent cash, assumed obligations or issued shares may overstate it. The supplied record gives no consideration or earnings figures, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing statement, consideration and funding mix, assumed liabilities, acquired working capital, share issuance and Homes Direct operating results; rebuild OE and the bridge on one post-closing perimeter.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains a tax credit that has been terminated
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $10.270m credit; computed $122.2m-$170.2m of operating value, or $2.21-$3.08 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The terminated credit increased FY2026 after-tax earnings embedded in the $204.4m OE anchor and is consequently compounded through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: OBBBA changed many aspects of U.S. corporate income taxation including accelerated bonus depreciation, research and experimentation expense deduction, and terminating the energy efficient home tax credit.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated recurring-earnings error: the credit equals 5.0% of anchor OE. Removing it proportionally from the supplied scenarios reduces values to approximately $56.08-$72.55 per share. Even the original $75.63 bull value was $12.13 below the $87.76 market price, so the correction cannot reverse the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove $10.270m from prospective OE, separately quantify sustainable OBBBA benefits, and rerun all three scenarios and the buy-below calculation.

audit_findings.title: Known water-intrusion liability may not be reconciled to the gross cash addition
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $29.320m latest liability; computed maximum direct bridge effect $0.53 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any remediation payments not already represented in forecast OE reduce cash attributable to common equity and should be deducted from the bridge; deducting payments already captured in OE would double-count them.
audit_findings.evidence: The actuarial analysis completed in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 resulted in a charge of $ 8.5 million to increase the remaining estimated liability to $ 35.6 million at March 28, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The reconciliation is unresolved, but the latest filed liability is $29.320m, down from $35.603m. Deducting the entire latest balance from equity value would reduce value by only $0.53 per share, about 0.8% of base equity value and far below the $12.13 gap between bull value and market price. Revisions beyond the recorded liability are not established by the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Trace remediation payments, the $2.5m purchase credits and other supplier reimbursements through historical and forecast OE; deduct only the present value not already captured in cash flows.

audit_findings.title: The interest-income purge may remove an operating financing business
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $2.900m FY2026 floor-plan interest income; computed 51% parent share $1.479m pre-tax and approximately $0.25-$0.35 per share of scenario value after the filed 21% tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Purging floor-plan lending interest as surplus-cash yield removes operating OE from Champion Financing; only the parent-attributable earnings after credit costs and servicing expenses belong in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest income from floor plan receivables for the year ended March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, was $ 2.9 million a nd $ 2.4 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the purge actually removed this income is unresolved, but its disclosed scale cannot change the conclusion. Applying the 51% ownership and FY2026 effective tax rate produces about $1.168m of annual parent-attributable after-tax income, worth approximately $13.9m-$19.4m, or $0.25-$0.35 per share, under the supplied scenario multiples.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the interest-income purge ledger and Champion Financing consolidation; restore only the 51% parent-attributable floor-plan earnings net of credit losses, funding and servicing costs.

audit_findings.title: A latest-year anchor may capitalize a bundle of transient items
audit_findings.magnitude: filed net $13.502m pre-tax for the named items; computed conservative upper-bound effect $160.6m-$223.8m, or $2.91-$4.06 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Transient expenses retained in OE understate the anchor, while a retained facility-sale gain overstates it; either treatment propagates through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Adjusted EBITDA is presented as a supplemental measure of the Company’s financial performance that management believes is useful to investors, because the excluded items may vary significantly in timing or amounts and/or may obscure trends useful in evaluating and comparing the Company’s operating activities across reporting periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The ledger treatment remains unresolved. The named FY2026 items comprise $4.496m contingent-consideration expense, $5.832m plant-closure costs, $5.030m net water cost and $1.794m transaction costs, offset by a $3.650m gain. Even applying the full $13.502m net amount to OE without a tax reduction gives an intentionally conservative maximum increase of $4.06 per share; bull value would remain about $8.07 below the market price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2026 OE adjustment ledger and normalize each named item symmetrically, confirming that noncash remeasurements, gains and accrued liabilities were not already removed through the cash-flow calculation.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized cloud-system spending could escape the reinvestment charge
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back cloud-software amortization without subtracting the related capitalized implementation cash outlays overstates distributable OE and its terminal capitalization.
audit_findings.evidence: The system selection and implementation process has required, and will continue to require, a significant investment of personnel and financial resources.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish $18.3m of net capitalized cloud costs at June 27, 2026 and $4.1m of FY2026 amortization, but they do not provide a cash-additions rollforward or the OE ledger. The record therefore cannot determine whether implementation spending was already captured in operating cash flow or separately deducted, or whether any omission is large enough to affect the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the cloud-cost rollforward and cash-flow classification, reconcile every capitalized implementation payment to OE, and rerun scenarios if amortization was added back without the corresponding cash reinvestment.
